title: Unsound Send and Sync Implementations
platform_conditions: Any Rust toolchain; the C11/C++-style memory model of std::sync::atomic Orderings applies per CPU architecture
security_mechanism: The compiler grants cross-thread access based on the marker traits Send and Sync, and `unsafe impl Sync for T` asserts to the whole type system that &T is thread-sharable without any proof: a type holding a raw pointer or a non-atomic counter then compiles into data races that are undefined behavior, not mere wrong answers. static mut shares the same hazard — every access is a raw multi-threaded pointer dereference with no synchronization. Relaxed or mis-chosen atomic Orderings compile but do not synchronize: a flag set with Relaxed and read with Relaxed may be observed late or reordered relative to the data it protects, so a check-then-act on credentials races with the writer. Across .await points the same state interleaves between polls, producing a check-then-act race the borrow checker cannot see.

source_sink_clues.source: Concurrent requests mutating shared authorization state, session tables, or caches; asynchronous tasks sharing one non-synchronized state object across .await points.
source_sink_clues.sink: unsafe impl Send/Sync for types containing raw pointers or non-atomic state; static mut access; atomics with incorrect Ordering guarding other data; Mutex-adjacent check-then-act sequences across .await

tracking_guards: Check that every unsafe impl Send/Sync is backed by an argument why &self is thread-safe (interior synchronization, immutable after construction), that static mut is replaced by OnceLock/lazy initialization or atomics, that an atomic Release/Acquire (not Relaxed) publishes the data it guards, and that shared state touched across .await is behind a Mutex or an actor owning the state.
not_candidate_when: The type is genuinely thread-safe (all fields atomic or behind locks) and the unsafe impl documents that proof, the state is only reachable from one thread/task by construction, or the atomic is used with an ordering that actually establishes the required happens-before relation.
synthetic_safe_example: /* use Mutex or Arc to ensure thread safety */
public_references: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/362.html
